static_findings.snippet: 本 SKILL 用于指导在 FlowGram 项目的 `@flowgram.ai/form-materials` 包中创建新的物料组件。
- ✅ **在现有包中创建**:直接在 `packages/materials/form-materials/src/components/` 下创建组件目录
- ✅ **通过类型检查**:必须通过 `yarn ts-check`
- **类型定义**:`IJsonSchema` 来自 `@flowgram.ai/json-schema`(不使用外部的 `json-schema` 包)
- **React**:必须显式 `import React` 避免 UMD 全局引用错误
然后编辑 `packages/materials/form-materials/src/index.ts`,确保新组件在主导出列表中:
- 使用 `type IJsonSchema` 而非 `type JSONSchema7`
- [ ] 通过 `yarn ts-check` 类型检查
访问 http://localhost:6006/,找到你的组件进行测试。

content.value_statement: FlowGram component work can require consistent exports, stories, and type checks. This skill provides a focused workflow for building form-material components within the existing package.
actual_capabilities: Defines the expected directory structure for a form-material component.
Provides React and TypeScript component patterns with named exports.
Explains how to add component exports at package entry points.
Shows how to create a Storybook story for manual testing.
Lists type-check and local development commands.
limitations: Applies specifically to the FlowGram form-materials package structure.
Does not generate production-ready component logic or tests.
Recommends manual Storybook testing instead of automated test coverage.
Requires an existing FlowGram repository and its project dependencies.

use_cases.title: Create a new form component
use_cases.description: Add a focused React material component with the required files, exports, and package integration.

use_cases.title: Prepare a component demo
use_cases.description: Create a Storybook story that demonstrates component behavior and captures callback results.

use_cases.title: Resolve integration issues
use_cases.description: Check React imports, export paths, and JSON schema types when a new component fails to build.

prompt_templates.title: Start a component
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan a new FlowGram form-material component named StatusBadge. List the files and required exports.

prompt_templates.title: Draft component files
prompt_templates.prompt: Create the TypeScript component, index file, and export changes for a FlowGram form-material component. Use named exports only.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Storybook demo
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a Storybook story for my new FlowGram component. Show its main interaction and display the callback result.

prompt_templates.title: Review package integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my FlowGram component changes against this skill. Check paths, exports, React imports, types, and type-check steps.

output_examples.input: My component is undefined in the demo.
output_examples.output: A checklist to verify the component index, components index, and package source index exports.

output_examples.input: React is reported as a UMD global.
output_examples.output: A recommendation to add an explicit React import at the top of the module.

best_practices: Keep each material component focused on one user task.
Use named exports and update every required package entry point.
Run the type check and test the component in Storybook before review.
anti_patterns: Do not create a separate package for a single material component.
Do not add optional props that are unrelated to the core function.
Do not skip export updates when adding a component.

faq.question: Which package does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets the FlowGram form-materials package and its existing component structure.

faq.question: Should I use default exports?
faq.answer: No. The guidance requires named exports for components and their types.

faq.question: How should I test a component?
faq.answer: Create a Storybook story, run the local development environment, and test the component manually.

faq.question: What type check should I run?
faq.answer: Run yarn ts-check from the form-materials package directory.

faq.question: Which JSON schema type should I import?
faq.answer: Import IJsonSchema from the FlowGram JSON schema package.

faq.question: Does this skill add automated tests?
faq.answer: No. It documents manual Storybook testing and does not provide automated test guidance.
